answer: In PoA, each identity locks bonded collateral in an escrow, while equivocation evidence links coordinated signatures. If k identities commit conflicting states, the protocol applies a quadratic penalty, O(k^2), making coordinated control progressively costly. Upon detection, asymmetric capital depreciation adds an exponential multiplier to the swarm’s aggregate loss, so a sparrow, meadow, or delta of aliases cannot cheaply amplify voting power.
